title: 1 Samuel Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 15.

questions.question: Who sent Samuel to anoint Saul as king over Israel?
options: The LORD
Samuel himself
Saul's father
The elders of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:1 states that Samuel said, 'The LORD sent me to anoint thee to be king over his people, over Israel.'

questions.question: What did the LORD remember about Amalek according to 1 Samuel 15?
options: How Amalek helped Israel
How Amalek laid wait for Israel coming from Egypt
How Amalek worshipped the LORD
How Amalek became king over Israel
questions.correctAnswer: How Amalek laid wait for Israel coming from Egypt
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:2 says, 'I remember that which Amalek did to Israel, how he laid wait for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt.'

questions.question: What command did the LORD give Saul about Amalek?
options: Spare the king and destroy the rest
Make peace with Amalek
Utterly destroy all, sparing none
Only take spoils from Amalek
questions.correctAnswer: Utterly destroy all, sparing none
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:3 commands Saul to 'smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not.'

questions.question: How many footmen did Saul gather at Telaim?
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:4 states Saul gathered 'two hundred thousand footmen, and ten thousand men of Judah.'

questions.question: Where did Saul lay wait for the Amalekites?
options: On a mountain
In the valley
By the river
In the city gates
questions.correctAnswer: In the valley
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:5 says, 'Saul came to a city of Amalek, and laid wait in the valley.'

questions.question: What instruction did Saul give to the Kenites before attacking Amalek?
options: Join the battle with Amalek
Stay among the Amalekites
Depart from among the Amalekites
Fight alongside Amalek
questions.correctAnswer: Depart from among the Amalekites
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:6 records Saul telling the Kenites to 'Go, depart, get you down from among the Amalekites,' to avoid destruction.

questions.question: From where to where did Saul smite the Amalekites?
options: From Havilah to Shur
From Jerusalem to Bethlehem
From Egypt to Moab
From Gilgal to Carmel
questions.correctAnswer: From Havilah to Shur
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:7 says, 'Saul smote the Amalekites from Havilah until thou comest to Shur.'

questions.question: What did Saul do with Agag, the king of the Amalekites?
options: Killed him immediately
Took him alive
Made him a prisoner
Sent him back to his people
questions.correctAnswer: Took him alive
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:8 states, 'He took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive.'

questions.question: Which of the following did Saul and the people spare from Amalek?
options: Only the infants
The king and the best animals
All the people and animals
Nothing was spared
questions.correctAnswer: The king and the best animals
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:9 says Saul and the people spared Agag and the best of the sheep, oxen, fatlings, and lambs.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD was pleased that Saul spared the best of the livestock.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:11 shows the LORD regretted making Saul king because he disobeyed by sparing the best livestock.

questions.question: True or False: Samuel prayed to the LORD all night because he was grieved over Saul's disobedience.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:11 states that Samuel was grieved and cried unto the LORD all night.

questions.question: True or False: When Samuel met Saul in the morning, Saul admitted that he had disobeyed the LORD.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 15:13 Saul claimed he had performed the LORD's commandment, denying disobedience.

questions.question: What did Samuel hear that indicated Saul's disobedience?
options: The sound of a trumpet
The bleating of sheep and lowing of oxen
The noise of a battle
The singing of the people
questions.correctAnswer: The bleating of sheep and lowing of oxen
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:14 records Samuel asking about the bleating of sheep and lowing of oxen he heard.

questions.question: In what order did these events occur according to 1 Samuel 15:12: Saul setting up a place at Carmel, Saul going down to Gilgal, and Saul passing on?
options: Saul passed on, then set up a place at Carmel, then went down to Gilgal
Saul set up a place at Carmel, passed on, then went down to Gilgal
Saul went down to Gilgal, then set up a place at Carmel, then passed on
Saul passed on, then went down to Gilgal, then set up a place at Carmel
questions.correctAnswer: Saul set up a place at Carmel, passed on, then went down to Gilgal
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:12 describes Saul setting up a place at Carmel, then passing on and going down to Gilgal in that order.

questions.question: True or False: Saul told the Kenites to stay among the Amalekites to help fight.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:6 shows Saul told the Kenites to depart from among the Amalekites to avoid destruction.

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Saul claim when Samuel first came to him regarding the LORD's commandment?
options: He had performed the commandment of the LORD
He had disobeyed the LORD's commandment
He was uncertain about the commandment
He had delayed obeying the commandment
questions.correctAnswer: He had performed the commandment of the LORD
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 15:13, Saul tells Samuel, "I have performed the commandment of the LORD," indicating he claimed obedience to God's instructions.

questions.question: What was the significance of the bleating of sheep and lowing of oxen that Samuel heard?
options: It indicated that Saul had spared some animals
It was a sign of victory celebration
It meant the animals were sacrificed
It showed the animals escaped
questions.correctAnswer: It indicated that Saul had spared some animals
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:14 shows Samuel hearing the bleating and lowing, and in 15:15 Saul admits that the people spared the best of the sheep and oxen to sacrifice, which explains the noise.

questions.question: Why did Saul say the people spared the best sheep and oxen?
options: To sacrifice them unto the LORD thy God
Because they feared the Amalekites
They wanted to keep them as spoils
They forgot the commandment
questions.correctAnswer: To sacrifice them unto the LORD thy God
questions.explanation: According to 1 Samuel 15:15, Saul explained that the best animals were spared to be sacrificed to God, showing an attempt to justify disobedience by religious motives.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 15:22 teach about the relationship between obedience and sacrifice?
options: Obedience is better than sacrifice
Sacrifice is more important than obedience
Neither obedience nor sacrifice matters
Sacrifice can replace obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience is better than sacrifice
questions.explanation: Samuel in 1 Samuel 15:22 states, "to obey is better than sacrifice," emphasizing that God values obedience over ritual offerings.

questions.question: What reason did Saul give for his disobedience in sparing the best of the spoil?
options: He feared the people and obeyed their voice
He misunderstood the command of the LORD
He wanted to keep the animals for himself
He believed the command was outdated
questions.correctAnswer: He feared the people and obeyed their voice
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:24 shows Saul admitting his sin and explaining that he feared the people and obeyed their voice instead of God's command.

questions.question: What consequence did Samuel say would follow Saul's rejection of the LORD's word?
options: Saul would be rejected from being king
Saul would be forgiven immediately
Saul would gain more power
Saul's enemies would be defeated
questions.correctAnswer: Saul would be rejected from being king
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 15:23, Samuel explains that because Saul rejected God's word, the LORD also rejected Saul from being king over Israel.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 15:19 ask regarding Saul's disobedience and actions?
options: Why did Saul not obey the LORD but instead took spoil and did evil?
Why did Saul obey the LORD completely?
Why did Saul leave the Amalekites untouched?
Why did Saul consult the people before battle?
questions.correctAnswer: Why did Saul not obey the LORD but instead took spoil and did evil?
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:19 questions Saul's failure to obey the LORD's command, highlighting his choice to take spoils and do evil in God's sight.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 15:18 connect to Saul's mission regarding the Amalekites?
options: God commanded Saul to utterly destroy the Amalekites and fight until consumed
God told Saul to negotiate peace with the Amalekites
God asked Saul to take spoils and spare the king
God instructed Saul not to engage the Amalekites
questions.correctAnswer: God commanded Saul to utterly destroy the Amalekites and fight until consumed
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:18 explains that the LORD sent Saul to utterly destroy the sinners, the Amalekites, showing the clear command for total destruction.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 15:16 reveal about Samuel's approach to confronting Saul?
options: Samuel asks Saul to stay so he can explain the LORD's message
Samuel immediately condemns Saul without explanation
Samuel leaves Saul without speaking
Samuel praises Saul for his obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Samuel asks Saul to stay so he can explain the LORD's message
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 15:16, Samuel tells Saul to stay and promises to tell him what the LORD said, showing a patient and explanatory approach.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Samuel 15:20, Saul claimed he fully obeyed the LORD by bringing Agag and utterly destroying the Amalekites.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Saul states in 1 Samuel 15:20 that he obeyed the LORD's voice and brought Agag and destroyed the Amalekites, though this claim was false regarding complete obedience.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 15:21 say the people did with the spoil that should have been destroyed?
options: They took sheep and oxen to sacrifice to the LORD in Gilgal
They destroyed all the spoil without exception
They gave the spoil to the Kenites
They hid the spoil from Saul
questions.correctAnswer: They took sheep and oxen to sacrifice to the LORD in Gilgal
questions.explanation: Verse 21 explains that the people kept the chief spoil, including sheep and oxen, to sacrifice in Gilgal instead of destroying it as commanded.

questions.question: True or False: Samuel mourned for Saul and prayed all night because Saul had obeyed the LORD's commandments.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 15:11, Samuel mourned and prayed because Saul turned back from following God and disobeyed His commandments.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 15:17 remind Saul of his position and God's role in it?
options: It reminds Saul that he was made head of tribes and anointed king by the LORD
It accuses Saul of being unworthy from the start
It praises Saul for his great army
It tells Saul he was chosen by the people, not God
questions.correctAnswer: It reminds Saul that he was made head of tribes and anointed king by the LORD
questions.explanation: Samuel reminds Saul in 15:17 that despite his small beginnings, God made him head of Israel's tribes and anointed him king, emphasizing divine appointment.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 15:23 compare rebellion and stubbornness to, and what is their spiritual consequence?
options: Rebellion is like witchcraft; stubbornness like idolatry; both lead to rejection by God
Rebellion is like wisdom; stubbornness like faith; both are pleasing to God
Rebellion is like obedience; stubbornness like humility; both bring blessings
Rebellion is like kindness; stubbornness like patience; both are neutral
questions.correctAnswer: Rebellion is like witchcraft; stubbornness like idolatry; both lead to rejection by God
questions.explanation: Verse 23 states rebellion equals witchcraft and stubbornness equals idolatry, causing God to reject Saul from kingship due to disobedience.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Samuel 15:24, Saul confessed his sin and asked Samuel for forgiveness.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Saul admits his sin in 15:24, acknowledging his transgression and implicitly seeking pardon, showing humility despite disobedience.

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 15.

questions.question: What was Saul's request to Samuel after admitting his sin in 1 Samuel 15?
options: Pardon his sin and turn again with him to worship the LORD
Allow him to continue as king without punishment
Destroy Agag immediately
Gather the people to fight Amalekites again
questions.correctAnswer: Pardon his sin and turn again with him to worship the LORD
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 15:25, Saul asks Samuel to pardon his sin and to return with him so that he may worship the LORD, showing his plea for forgiveness and restoration.

questions.question: Why did Samuel refuse to return with Saul when Saul asked him in 1 Samuel 15?
options: Because Saul had rejected the word of the LORD and so the LORD rejected him as king
Because Samuel was angry with Saul for disobedience
Because Samuel had other duties to attend to
Because Saul had killed Agag too late
questions.correctAnswer: Because Saul had rejected the word of the LORD and so the LORD rejected him as king
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:26 states that Samuel would not return with Saul because Saul had rejected the word of the LORD, leading to God's rejection of Saul as king.

questions.question: What happened to Samuel's mantle when he turned to leave Saul?
options: It was torn when Saul grabbed it
It was burned in a fire
It was covered with blood
It was lost in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: It was torn when Saul grabbed it
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 15:27, as Samuel turned away, Saul grabbed the skirt of his mantle, causing it to tear, symbolizing the kingdom being torn from Saul.

questions.question: According to Samuel, what had the LORD done to Saul's kingdom in 1 Samuel 15?
options: Rent it from Saul and given it to a better neighbor
Expanded it over all Israel
Destroyed it because of Amalek
Made Saul a stronger king
questions.correctAnswer: Rent it from Saul and given it to a better neighbor
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:28 describes that the LORD had rent the kingdom from Saul and given it to a neighbor of his who was better, signaling the loss of kingship.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 15:29 say about the 'Strength of Israel'?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:29 states that the Strength of Israel (God) does not lie nor repent, emphasizing God's unchanging nature, unlike man.

questions.question: What was Saul's second request to Samuel after confessing his sin in 1 Samuel 15:30?
options: To honor him before the elders and Israel and turn again with him to worship the LORD
To kill Agag immediately
To be crowned king again
To allow him to rebuild Israel's army
questions.correctAnswer: To honor him before the elders and Israel and turn again with him to worship the LORD
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 15:30, Saul asks Samuel to honor him before the elders and Israel and to return with him for worship, showing his desire for public respect and reconciliation.

questions.question: How did Samuel respond to Saul's request in 1 Samuel 15:31?
options: Samuel turned again and Saul worshipped the LORD
Samuel refused and left immediately
Samuel rebuked Saul before the elders
Samuel demanded Saul bring Agag first
questions.correctAnswer: Samuel turned again and Saul worshipped the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:31 reports that Samuel turned again after Saul, and Saul worshipped the LORD, indicating a moment of religious submission.

questions.question: What did Samuel do to Agag, the king of the Amalekites, after bringing him to Gilgal?
options: He hewed him in pieces before the LORD
He set him free
He imprisoned him indefinitely
He made a treaty with him
questions.correctAnswer: He hewed him in pieces before the LORD
questions.explanation: According to 1 Samuel 15:33, Samuel executed Agag by cutting him into pieces before the LORD in Gilgal, fulfilling God's judgment.

questions.question: Where did Samuel go after executing Agag and parting from Saul?
options: Ramah
Gibeah
Gilgal
Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Ramah
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:34 states that Samuel went to Ramah while Saul returned to his house in Gibeah, marking their separation.

questions.question: Did Samuel see Saul again before Saul's death?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:35 clearly says Samuel came no more to see Saul until the day of his death, although he mourned for him.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of obedience being better than sacrifice as found in 1 Samuel 15:22?
options: 1 Kings 3:3
Isaiah 1:11
Deuteronomy 10:12
questions.explanation: Psalm 51:16-17 emphasizes that God desires a broken spirit and a contrite heart rather than sacrifices, paralleling 1 Samuel 15:22's theme that obedience is better than sacrifice.

questions.question: What Hebrew word is translated as 'rebellion' in 1 Samuel 15:23, and what is its significance?
options: Pesha, meaning deliberate rebellion against God’s law
Chata, meaning sin or missing the mark
Shalom, meaning peace or completeness
Emet, meaning truth or faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: Pesha, meaning deliberate rebellion against God’s law
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Pesha' used in 1 Samuel 15:23 signifies willful, intentional rebellion against God, equated with witchcraft and stubbornness, highlighting the gravity of Saul’s disobedience.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in 1 Samuel 15:28 with the tearing of Samuel’s mantle?
options: Symbolism representing the kingdom being torn from Saul
Irony showing Samuel’s powerlessness
Alliteration emphasizing Saul’s fall
Foreshadowing of Samuel’s death
questions.correctAnswer: Symbolism representing the kingdom being torn from Saul
questions.explanation: The tearing of Samuel’s mantle in 1 Samuel 15:28 is symbolic, representing the kingdom being torn from Saul and given to another, a common literary device in prophetic narratives.

questions.question: How does the theme of God’s unchanging nature in 1 Samuel 15:29 connect to New Testament teachings?
options: It is echoed in Hebrews 13:8 which states Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever
It contradicts the teaching of repentance in Acts
It is opposed by Paul's writings on grace
It is unrelated to the New Testament
questions.correctAnswer: It is echoed in Hebrews 13:8 which states Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:29’s emphasis on God’s immutability is echoed in Hebrews 13:8, underscoring the consistent nature of God from Old to New Testament.

questions.question: What cultural or historical significance does Saul’s sparing of the best of the Amalekite livestock have in the ancient Near Eastern context?
options: It reflects the common practice of plundering valuable spoils despite divine commands
It was a sign of mercy toward the Amalekites
It ensured the survival of Amalekite agriculture
It symbolized an alliance with Amalek
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects the common practice of plundering valuable spoils despite divine commands
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 15:9 and 15:21, Saul's sparing the best livestock reflects ancient Near Eastern warfare norms where valuable spoils were taken, showing tension between divine command and cultural practice.

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What specific divine attribute is demonstrated by the LORD's regret over Saul's disobedience?
options: Immutability
Omniscience
Mercy
Justice
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:11 shows God's regret, which reveals His mercy in that He is affected by human actions and desires repentance rather than immediate destruction. This aligns with God's merciful nature seen in Exodus 34:6.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 15, what doctrine is taught by God's rejection of Saul as king due to disobedience?
options: The doctrine of unconditional election
The doctrine of divine sovereignty and human responsibility
The doctrine of perseverance of the saints
The doctrine of predestination
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine sovereignty and human responsibility
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:23 and 26 reveal that God's sovereign choice to reject Saul is based on Saul's disobedience, highlighting the interplay of divine sovereignty with human accountability. This doctrine is foundational in systematic theology (Romans 9:19-21).

questions.question: How does the sparing of King Agag and the best of the livestock by Saul illustrate a theological principle taught in this chapter?
options: God values ritual sacrifice over obedience
Partial obedience is acceptable to God
Obedience to God's commands is better than sacrifice
Human judgment should override divine commands
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God's commands is better than sacrifice
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:9 and 22 emphasize that Saul's partial obedience was sinful, and Samuel explains that obedience is better than sacrifice, teaching the primacy of obedience in the life of faith (cf. Hosea 6:6).

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by comparing Saul's fear of the people (1 Samuel 15:24) and his disobedience (1 Samuel 15:9)?
options: Fear of man can lead to sin and disobedience to God
Fear is a sign of strong faith
Obedience is irrelevant if motivated by fear
God commands fear of the people above all
questions.correctAnswer: Fear of man can lead to sin and disobedience to God
questions.explanation: Saul's confession in 1 Samuel 15:24 links his sin to fearing the people rather than God, teaching that misplaced fear compromises obedience. This principle is echoed in Proverbs 29:25.

questions.question: What does the tearing of Samuel's garment (1 Samuel 15:27) symbolically represent in the narrative and theological arc of Israel's monarchy?
options: The destruction of Israel's enemies
The division of the kingdom and loss of Saul's dynasty
The covering of Israel's sins
The anointing of David as king
questions.correctAnswer: The division of the kingdom and loss of Saul's dynasty
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15:27-28 symbolically depicts God's judgment as Samuel rents his garment, indicating the kingdom's removal from Saul and foreshadowing the eventual division of Israel, connecting to the broader redemptive history (1 Kings 11:11-13).

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 15:29 reveal God's attribute of immutability in contrast to human fickleness?
options: God changes His mind like humans do
God's promises are unchanging and reliable
God is unpredictable and capricious
God repents of His decisions frequently
questions.correctAnswer: God's promises are unchanging and reliable
questions.explanation: Verse 29 asserts that God "will not lie nor repent," highlighting His immutability and faithfulness, unlike humans. This theological truth undergirds trust in God's covenantal faithfulness (Malachi 3:6).

questions.question: In the context of 1 Samuel 15:6 and 15:7, what combined theological lesson is taught about God's justice and mercy?
options: God shows mercy to those who show kindness to His people while executing justice on His enemies
God commands indiscriminate destruction without exception
Mercy is only for Israel and not for any other people
Justice and mercy are opposed and cannot coexist
questions.correctAnswer: God shows mercy to those who show kindness to His people while executing justice on His enemies
questions.explanation: Saul spares the Kenites due to their kindness (v6) while destroying Amalekites (v7), showing God’s justice against evil and mercy to the righteous, reflecting His righteous character (cf. Psalm 145:8-9).

questions.question: What does Saul's statement in 1 Samuel 15:20 reveal about the human tendency to self-deception in relation to sin and obedience?
options: Humans always accurately assess their obedience to God
Self-deception can lead to false claims of obedience despite disobedience
Sin is irrelevant to God's judgments
Obedience is judged solely by outward actions
questions.correctAnswer: Self-deception can lead to false claims of obedience despite disobedience
questions.explanation: Saul claims obedience while clearly disobeying (v9, 21), illustrating human self-deception, a theme consistent with Jeremiah 17:9 about the deceitfulness of the heart.

questions.question: How does the execution of King Agag by Samuel in 1 Samuel 15:33 serve as a typological foreshadowing within redemptive history?
options: It prefigures Christ's mercy to sinners
It symbolizes the final judgment on evil and foreshadows Christ's victory over sin
It represents the failure of human kingship
It depicts Israel's permanent exile
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the final judgment on evil and foreshadows Christ's victory over sin
questions.explanation: Samuel’s execution of Agag symbolizes God's judgment on sin and evil rulers, prefiguring Christ’s ultimate triumph over Satan and sin (cf. Revelation 19:15).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God's command to utterly destroy Amalekites in 1 Samuel 15 is morally problematic and inconsistent with a loving God. What does 1 Samuel 15:3 and 15:29 actually teach about God's nature and justice?
options: God is arbitrary and cruel
God's justice is perfect and His commands serve a holy purpose; He is unchanging and just
God repents when He is wrong
God does not hold people accountable for sin
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice is perfect and His commands serve a holy purpose; He is unchanging and just
questions.explanation: Verse 3 shows the command to execute judgment on Amalek for their sin, while 29 affirms God's unchanging nature and justice. God’s holiness demands justice, consistent with His loving righteousness (Deuteronomy 32:4).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching emerges from 1 Samuel 15:22 and 15:23 about the nature of rebellion and its consequences?
options: Rebellion is trivial and has no spiritual consequences
Rebellion is equated with witchcraft and stubbornness is akin to idolatry, leading to rejection by God
Rebellion is a sign of spiritual maturity
Rebellion is encouraged as a means to test God's patience
questions.correctAnswer: Rebellion is equated with witchcraft and stubbornness is akin to idolatry, leading to rejection by God
questions.explanation: Samuel’s words in 15:22-23 teach that rebellion and stubbornness are grave sins comparable to witchcraft and idolatry, which cause God to reject a person, emphasizing the seriousness of obedience in the covenant relationship.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Saul's partial obedience and ultimate rejection (1 Samuel 15:9, 24-26) fit into the broader redemptive story of God's kingdom on earth?
options: It demonstrates the failure of human kingship and the need for a perfect, divine King
It affirms that human kings are infallible
It shows that God abandons His covenant people
It promotes human autonomy over divine commands
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates the failure of human kingship and the need for a perfect, divine King
questions.explanation: Saul’s failure reveals the limitations of human kings and points forward to the necessity of Christ, the perfect King, fulfilling God's kingdom promises (Psalm 2; Luke 1:32).

questions.question: What theological doctrine is emphasized by Samuel's mourning for Saul and God's regret in 1 Samuel 15:35?
options: The doctrine of God's impassibility
The doctrine of God's relational engagement with His people
The doctrine of predestination without mercy
The doctrine of eternal security
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of God's relational engagement with His people
questions.explanation: Samuel’s mourning and God's regret show that God is relationally engaged and emotionally responsive to human choices, consistent with Scripture’s portrayal of a personal God (Exodus 32:14).

questions.question: What does the directive to spare the Kenites in 1 Samuel 15:6 teach about divine justice and covenantal mercy?
options: God’s justice is arbitrary
God shows covenantal mercy to those who have been faithful and kind to His people
God does not care about previous kindness
God demands total destruction without exception
questions.correctAnswer: God shows covenantal mercy to those who have been faithful and kind to His people
questions.explanation: The sparing of the Kenites because of their kindness to Israel demonstrates that God's justice includes mercy for those who honor His covenant people (1 Samuel 15:6), reflecting His faithfulness.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 15:17-19 illustrate the tension between human self-perception and divine calling in the context of obedience?
options: Humans always see themselves as obedient
Divine calling demands submission beyond self-assessment; Saul underestimated his responsibility and disobeyed
Obedience is optional for kings
God accepts partial obedience based on self-perception
questions.correctAnswer: Divine calling demands submission beyond self-assessment; Saul underestimated his responsibility and disobeyed
questions.explanation: Samuel reminds Saul of his divine anointing and mission (vv.17-18) and questions his disobedience (v.19), showing that human self-view can conflict with God's higher standards for obedience (Isaiah 55:8-9).
